svg.text: Replayer protocol — startup integrity, cold-start walk, live-tap follow, gap recovery, refusal & stall
ReplayerStreamReceiver (C++) ↔ ReplayerService (Java) — node-local aeron:ipc, streams 201/202/203/204/205
LOOP
per remaining recording segment
LOOP
~500ms, for as long as the image is held
ALT
alt — the resumed replay opened on the wrong frame, or the Replayer refuses the
position (it predates the active recording, or the recording rotated under it and
answers NO_REPLAY_NEEDED over a hole we know is open)
Startup — the Replayer proves its own history before it serves any of it
startReplay(span, span.startPosition, 4096 bytes) [stream 204]
one span per duty cycle, never blocking one
first frame of the span [stream 204]
every recording in this node's chain must open at globalSeqNo=1 — recovery is always full-log replay, so a span
that starts higher resumed mid-history and IS a hole at its join. ready (phixeron.replayer.ready) is set only once
the whole chain is proved; until then every request is answered ReplayPending. A span that opens higher latches
integrityFailed for this process's lifetime and every request is answered ReplayUnavailable.
Cold start — walk the node's recording chain (segmentIndex 0, 1, 2, ...)
ReplayRequest(clientId, requestId=1, segmentIndex=0,
fromPosition=0)
startReplay(chain[0], its startPosition, bounded to the recording tip)
Replaying(requestId=1, replaySessionId, catchUpPosition=tip, recordingId=R0)
subscribes to stream 201 filtered to ?session-id=<replaySessionId>, for only as long as it rides this
replay — a standing subscription made every idle app a non-polling subscriber of every other app's replay
replay frames [stream 201]
rides the image to catchUpPosition (a bounded replay of an ACTIVE recording never closes its image at
the bound); the live tap is drained AND dispatched in parallel — frames beyond this segment are
retained in the bounded globalSeqNo-ordered ahead-buffer (MAX_MESSAGES_FRAMES / MAX_MESSAGES_BYTES),
not dropped
ReplayRequest(requestId+1, segmentIndex+1, fromPosition=0)
the Replayer resolves the segment's own startPosition
Replaying(requestId, replaySessionId, catchUpPosition, recordingId=Rn)
recordingId different from the one this segmentIndex resolved to before -> the chain shifted under the
walk (a stale span dropped by ReplayRecordings.stitch) -> abandon it and re-walk from segment 0
Replaying(requestId, replaySessionId=NO_REPLAY_NEEDED, recordingId=Rn >= 0)
NO_REPLAY_NEEDED that still NAMES a recording = that segment is empty (an unclean restart created it
before anything was published): skip it and request segmentIndex+1. Ending the walk here would
truncate the whole chain.
Replaying(requestId=N, replaySessionId=NO_REPLAY_NEEDED, recordingId=-1)
no recording named — the chain is exhausted, and only this ends a walk
drain the ahead-buffer first: anything still retained behind a hole, or a latched overflow, means the
frontier is short of the real one -> re-walk from segment 0 instead. Otherwise isCaughtUp()=true and
the app follows the live tap directly. No ReplayComplete — the walk-terminating request already
freed the slot.
Steady state — following the live tap
frame gseq=104
in order (gseq == last+1) — dispatched
Gap detected -> resume -> ahead-buffer closes the seam
frame gseq=106 (expected 105)
isCaughtUp() <- false (consumers gate on it: leader-only emission, the gateway's tap-stall watchdog)
· retains gseq=106 in the ahead-buffer instead of dropping it
ReplayRequest(requestId=k, segmentIndex=-1,
fromPosition=posOf(gseq=104)) — resume
startReplay(active recording, fromPosition, bounded to tip)
Replaying(requestId=k, replaySessionId, catchUpPosition=tip, recordingId)
ReplayHeartbeat(clientId) — refreshes the slot's 60s idle TTL
replay frame gseq=105 [stream 201]
anchor check: the FIRST replayed frame must be gseq=105, the frame the position was anchored on ->
dispatch 105, then drain the ahead-buffer -> dispatch retained gseq=106 — no further gap
at the tip, same guard as the walk terminator: drain, and re-walk from segment 0 if anything is still
retained or an overflow was latched — only then is the frontier real
ReplayComplete(clientId) — frees the slot at once (re-sent until it lands)
isCaughtUp() <- true (OnCaughtUp re-fires); back on the live tap
ReplayRequest(segmentIndex=0, fromPosition=0) — fall back
to a full chain re-walk, which needs no position to be sound
Replayer cannot serve — the app holds, and dispatches nothing
ReplayRequest(requestId=n, segmentIndex=s, fromPosition=p)
ReplayPending(requestId=n) — chain not proved ready yet, no free slot
(MAX_CONCURRENT_REPLAYS=4), local archive STALLED, nothing recorded yet,
or the recording's tip unreadable
holds at the gap; the ~500ms resend timer is the retry. A request queued for a slot is served the
moment one frees (drainPending on release/reclaim), not at the next sweep.
startReplay(active recording, 4096 bytes) [stream 204] — while STALLED,
at most one probe a second
probes with a replay, not a listing: serving a replay is what STALLED claims the archive cannot do.
An idle Replayer must not go on reporting a fault that ended hours ago, so phixeron.replayer.stalled
clears here rather than only on some app's next request.
ReplayUnavailable(requestId=n) — this node's chain failed the globalSeqNo-1 integrity sweep
no valid history to serve, so the app never goes caught up and every consumer gate stays shut.
Deliberately NOT fatal on either side: repair the archive and restart the Replayer — the resend timer
resumes it, with no app restart.
A replay that stops under us — re-request the same segment verbatim
ReplayRequest(requestId=n+1, same segmentIndex, same fromPosition)
no progress for 5s (REPLAY_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS), or the image closed SHORT of catchUpPosition — only a
close AT the bound is completion; advancing there would skip a segment that was never fully replayed.
A resume re-anchors instead of re-sending its stale position verbatim.
Recovery that never converges — alarmed, not fenced
app side: PROGRESS, not elapsed time — a legitimate cold start
replays the whole log and has no time bound, but a converging
recovery always advances globalSeqNo. Nothing dispatched in order
for 30s (RECOVERY_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_MS) while !isCaughtUp() -> a
fault line naming the state (segment, awaiting, session,
replayerUnavailable) + phixeron.app.recoveryStalled=1, cleared on
the next in-order dispatch. Holding is still the right response to
a baseline this node cannot establish; the alarm only says so.
Replayer side, same class of silence: two co-located apps launched
with one PHIXERON_REPLAYER_CLIENT_ID supersede each other's replay
on every request and neither ever catches up. 3 backwards requestId
steps within 10s separate that from a restart (exactly one) ->
phixeron.replayer.clientIdCollision=1. Reported, not refused: both
are already livelocked, and a false positive would stop a healthy
replica from ever recovering.
